cells.tense: You're tending it right now, and you know the tending is the point.
cells.verb: keeping both things alive at once
cells.place: in the small daily practice that nobody claps for
cells.ask: Let what you've finished be finished, and let the finishing feel like enough: hand over one thing this week without checking whether it held, so the care you've carried can turn into something you're free to do next.
cells.core: You're carrying two things that both matter, and you're carrying them on purpose rather than dropping one. Not by force — by showing up to the same small work again and again until it holds. That kind of care doesn't announce itself. It's why the thing is still standing.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping both of them alive, and the keeping is the work.

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead is the version where everything is finally handled, and you're already living there.
cells.verb: getting ahead of what will grow on its own time
cells.place: in a practice you keep pushing past what it can hold
cells.ask: Take one thing you're holding and let it finish on its own schedule — then let the satisfaction of it having been fully imagined arrive before you imagine the next: the vision you're chasing is downstream of something you haven't let yourself feel yet.
cells.core: You're tending everything at once, and you're tending it before it's here. The care that was supposed to be steady has become a grip — checking, correcting, getting ahead of what hasn't gone wrong yet. You're exhausted by a harvest that hasn't been planted. The thing you're protecting is being squeezed by the protecting.
cells.sheetLine: You're taking care of things before they need it, and it's costing you.

cells.tense: You stopped tending it a while back, and part of you is still standing at the door deciding whether to go in.
cells.place: at the edge of a discipline that used to be yours
cells.ask: Pick up one small piece of the practice again — not because you feel like it, but because you keep hoping something is still there; that hope is the fuel, and it's already in you, so let it light one session and let what you've built start to show.
cells.core: The light you used to keep lit is out, and you've told yourself it doesn't matter. But you keep thinking about it — a small, steady pull that you've been calling a phase or a past season. What's missing isn't the will to do the work. It's the belief that anything is waiting on the other side of starting again.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped tending it, and you keep thinking about it.

cells.tense: You're at the desk already, pen moving, but you talk about it like someone else is doing the writing.
cells.verb: shaping the thing without saying you're shaping it
cells.place: in the quiet work you've been calling just getting through
cells.ask: Say out loud that it's yours — one thing you've been treating as just the day's demands, the habit, the routine; name it as yours, and let that naming be the acknowledgment you've been waiting for from somewhere else.
cells.core: You've been tending it every day — the small disciplines, the keeping-things-together, the forms that hold the shape of what you care about. But when you describe your life, that work shows up as just how things are, not as something you're doing. The care is running the whole time. You just haven't claimed it. And you've been waiting for someone to notice the sacrifice before you'd let yourself call it one.
cells.sheetLine: You're already doing it. You just haven't said so.
